name: Akira
description: Akira is a prolific RaaS operation that ranked among the most active ransomware groups in 2025, reportedly extorting approximately $244M from 600+ victims. The group is notable for a rapid 'scan, steal, encrypt' lifecycle and for prioritizing backup infrastructure destruction early in intrusions to prevent victim recovery. In 2026 the group shifted away from experimental Rust code back to a faster, more stable C++ encryptor, reflecting a pragmatic tooling philosophy focused on operational efficiency.

detection_opportunities: Alert on VPN authentication from new devices or unusual geolocations
Detect VSS deletion and backup software termination commands
Monitor for ESXi and Hyper-V encryption activity
Alert on RClone or WinRAR usage in bulk data staging contexts

response_playbook: Audit and rotate VPN/appliance credentials and secrets â€” Akira frequently relies on retained config artifacts and valid accounts for initial access (T1190/T1078).
Check backup infrastructure and recovery tooling first â€” Akira prioritizes destroying backups (VSS deletion, backup software disabling) early in the intrusion.
Hunt for ESXi/Hyper-V hypervisor encryption activity to scope the blast radius across virtualized infrastructure.
Audit for RClone or WinRAR usage in bulk data-staging contexts indicating pre-encryption exfiltration.
Look for unauthorized AnyDesk installations and PsExec/SSH lateral movement on Linux/ESXi hosts.
Disable or restrict legitimate remote-access and file-compression tools where security tooling was found disabled (T1562.001).
Configure EDR solutions to remain active or alert during Safe Mode boots
Monitor for unexpected system reboots into Safe Mode via Windows event logs
Implement registry protections to prevent unauthorized Safe Mode configuration changes
Hunt for signs of data exfiltration even when ransomware encryption does not complete
